Ronald Reagan. The fortieth President of the United States, serving from 1981 to 1989, and a transformative conservative figure who reshaped American politics and foreign policy. An actor-turned-politician, he championed free-market economics known as Reaganomics, military strength against the Soviet Union, and a rollback of the welfare state, with his presidency coinciding with the final phase of the Cold War.

A former Hollywood actor and Democratic supporter who became a Republican in the 1960s, Reagan governed California from 1967 to 1975 as a conservative, building a coalition of social conservatives, anti-Communists, and free-market advocates. He was elected president in 1980 on a platform of tax cuts, deregulation, and aggressive anti-Communism, defeating incumbent Jimmy Carter with 51 percent of the vote. He won a landslide re-election in 1984.

He implemented Reaganomics through massive tax cuts for the wealthy on the theory that growth would trickle down, deregulation, and cuts to social programs. The economy recovered from 1982 onward, though inequality increased. He pursued a muscular anti-Communist foreign policy worldwide, supporting right-wing insurgencies in Nicaragua, Angola, and Afghanistan by arming the Mujahideen against the Soviets, and intervening in Grenada and Lebanon.

The Iran-Contra scandal involved his administration secretly selling arms to Iran despite an embargo and funneling proceeds to Contra insurgents in Nicaragua, violating Congressional restrictions. The scandal was contained, but the illegality was proven. He met Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev four times; initially hostile, calling the Soviet Union an evil empire, he shifted to engagement as Gorbachev pursued reform through glasnost and perestroika. Their summits reduced Cold War tensions and enabled arms control agreements.

He delivered the famous Tear Down This Wall speech at the Brandenburg Gate in 1987, calling on Gorbachev to remove the Berlin Wall, a symbolic moment preceding the Cold War's end. He won strong approval ratings and cultivated a Morning in America image, using optimistic rhetoric about American renewal.
